Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 1:

﴿O mankind﴾, that is, O people of Makkah. ﴿Fear your Lord, who created you from one soul﴾, that is, Adam. ﴿And created from it its mate﴾, that is, Hawwa' (Eve), who was created from one of his ribs. ﴿And spread forth from both of them﴾: that is, scattered and dispersed. ﴿And fear Allah﴾, that is, fear Him and obey Him. ﴿Through whom you ask one another﴾: that is, you ask one another for your needs and rights by Him, and say: "I ask you by Allah" and "I adjure you by Allah." As for His saying ﴿and the wombs﴾: that is, fear severing the ties of the wombs (al-arham, the ties of kinship) by cutting them off. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Watchful over you﴾: that is, a Guardian who observes your deeds, so fear Him regarding what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 2:

﴿And give the orphans their property.﴾ The address is to the guardians and custodians, i.e., give them their property when they reach maturity. ﴿And do not substitute the bad [property] (of yours)﴾ from their property, the unlawful, ﴿for the good﴾ lawful from your own property. This refers to the practice whereby the guardian of an orphan would take the good of the orphan's property and put in its place the inferior. ﴿And do not consume their property along with your property.﴾ Do not add it to your consumption alongside your own property when you are in need of it. ﴿Indeed, it﴾ i.e., indeed, consuming their property ﴿is a great sin﴾ i.e., a great offense.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 3:

﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly﴾: that you will not be just ﴿with the orphans﴾ (i.e., in marrying orphans), and that concerns you, ﴿then marry what seems good to you﴾, meaning: the good ones ﴿of women﴾, meaning: those who are lawful, apart from the forbidden ones. The meaning is: God, glorified is He, said to us: just as you fear that you will not be just among orphans when you take responsibility for them, then also fear that you will not be just among women when you marry them. So marry women ﴿two﴾, meaning: two and two, ﴿and three﴾, meaning: three and three, ﴿and four﴾, meaning: four and four. ﴿But if you fear that you will not be just﴾, meaning: among the four, ﴿then one﴾, meaning: let each one of you marry one woman. ﴿That﴾, meaning: marrying these women, despite their small number, ﴿is closer﴾, meaning: nearer, ﴿to avoiding injustice﴾, which is His saying: ﴿that you not deviate﴾, meaning: that you not incline away or act unjustly.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 4:

﴿And give the women their dowries (ṣadaqāt), O husbands, as a gift (niḥlah) with obligation and religious duty.﴾ Then ﴿if they willingly remit to you﴾, meaning: if their own selves are pleased to give you ﴿something﴾ of the dowry, ﴿then consume it with enjoyment (hanīʾan)﴾ in this world, with no authority (sulṭān) compelling you to it, ﴿and with ease (marīʾan)﴾ in the Hereafter, for God will not hold you accountable for it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 5:

﴿And do not give the feeble-minded﴾ — that is, the women and the children — ﴿your wealth, which Allah has made for you a means of sustenance﴾ — for your livelihood and the well-being of your worldly life. He says: Do not deliberately give your wealth, which Allah has entrusted to you and made a means of living for you, to your wife and your sons, so that they become the ones who stand over you (in charge of you), and then you look to what is in their hands. Rather, keep your wealth and manage it well, and be the one who spends on them in their clothing and provision. This is His saying: ﴿And provide for them from it﴾ (i.e., make for them a provision from it) ﴿and clothe them, and speak to them a kind word﴾ — that is, a good promise of goodness and kindness.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 6:

﴿And test the orphans⦆ i.e., test them in their intellects and their religious commitment. ﴿Until, when they reach marriageable age⦆ i.e., the time of marriage, meaning puberty through wet dreams. ﴿And if you perceive in them maturity⦆ i.e., you see in them ṣalāḥ (soundness) of intellect and preservation of property. ﴿And do not consume their property wastefully and hastily, fearing that they will grow up⦆ i.e., do not rush to consume their property before they grow up and attain maturity, fearing that they will reach adulthood and you will then be obliged to hand the property over to them. ﴿Whoever is wealthy⦆ among the guardians ﴿let him abstain⦆ from the orphan's property and not consume anything from it. ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat according to what is customary⦆ — he should fix a fair wage for his work. ﴿And when you hand over⦆ O guardians ﴿to them⦆ to the orphans ﴿their property, then have witnesses against them⦆ so that if a dispute arises, the guardian can establish proof of returning the property to them. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner⦆ — as one who calls to account and recompenses the doer of good and the doer of evil.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 7:

﴿For men there is a share﴾ (the verse). The Arabs in the pre-Islamic period (jahiliyyah) did not give inheritance to women or to young children anything. So God nullified that practice and made known that the right of inheritance is as stated in this verse, as an obligatory portion (fard).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 8:

﴿And when the distribution is attended by the relatives, the orphans, and the needy﴾ — that is, the division of the wealth among the heirs. ﴿Those of kinship﴾ — that is, those who are excluded from inheritance and do not inherit. ﴿The orphans and the needy, so provide for them from it﴾ — and this is by way of recommendation and encouragement: it is recommended for the heir to give a portion (raḍkh) to these people when they attend the division, from the gold and silver, and to speak to them a kind word (qawlan ma'rufan) when the inheritance is of a kind from which no portion can be given, such as land and slaves.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 9:

﴿And let those fear [Allah] who, were they to leave behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them.﴾ That is: let whoever has young children, and fears for them the loss (al-ḍay'a) after his death, fear that the testator might instruct that much be spent on the orphans, the needy and his relatives who do not inherit, so that he would have commanded him to do what he would not have done had he himself been the one who died. This was before the bequest was limited to a third (al-thuluth). His saying ﴿weak offspring﴾ means: young children; ﴿who would be anxious for them﴾ means: for fear of poverty. ﴿So let them fear Allah﴾ regarding what they say to one who is present at death; ﴿and let them speak words of rectitude﴾ meaning justice, which is that he should instruct him to leave his wealth to his children and give in charity less than a third, or a third. Then he mentioned the threat concerning consuming the property of orphans unjustly, saying:

Verse 10 of Surah an-Nisa' (4): "Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will [soon] burn in a Blaze."

"...the verse; its consequence leads to the Fire." "And they will burn in a Blaze": a fire of blazing flame, meaning they will suffer its heat and its intensity.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 11:

﴿Allah enjoins upon you﴾, i.e., He obligates you, for the wasiyya (bequest/injunction) from Allah is an obligation. ﴿Concerning your children﴾, the males and the females: ﴿for the male, the like of the portion of two females. And if they are women above two﴾, i.e., the children, ﴿above two﴾ here, "above" is a connective particle [şila] for "two." ﴿The two females inherit two-thirds by consensus today﴾, and that is His saying: ﴿then for them is two-thirds of what he left﴾. It is permissible to call the two by the plural. ﴿And if she is one﴾, the one left behind, ﴿then for her is half﴾. The explanation of the children's inheritance is complete. Then He said: ﴿And for his parents﴾, i.e., for the two parents of the deceased, ﴿for each one of them is a sixth of what he left, if he has a child. But if he has no child and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is a third. But if he has﴾, i.e., the deceased, ﴿siblings﴾, meaning two siblings, because the community has unanimously agreed that two siblings reduce the mother's share from a third to a sixth. And His saying: ﴿after any bequest﴾, i.e., these shares are only distributed after the settlement of debts and the execution of the deceased's bequest. ﴿Your fathers and your sons—you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾ in this world, so that you would give them from the inheritance what they deserve. But Allah has prescribed the obligations according to what is with Him of wisdom; had He left that to you, you would not have known which of them is more beneficial to you, and you would have corrupted and wasted. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing﴾ of things before their creation, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He has ordained of the obligations.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 12:

And His saying: ﴿And if a man leaves property to be inherited, [he having] no ascendants or descendants (kalalah)﴾. Kalalah: one who has neither a child nor a parent. Every heir who is neither a parent nor a child of the deceased is also a kalalah. The word kalalah in this verse refers to the deceased, meaning: if a man dies leaving no child and no parent, ﴿and he has a brother or a sister﴾, meaning from the mother, by the consensus of the Muslim community, ﴿then each one of them receives a sixth﴾, which is the prescribed share of one son of the mother, ﴿but if they are more than one﴾, they share in the third, the male and the female being equal in it. And His saying: ﴿without causing harm﴾, meaning: bringing harm upon the heirs, which is that he bequeaths a debt that he does not owe, intending thereby to harm the heirs. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ regarding what He has ordained of these prescribed shares, ﴿Forbearing﴾ toward whoever disobeys Him by delaying His punishment.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 15:

﴿And those who commit immorality among your women﴾ — they commit fornication (al-zina). ﴿Then bring against them four witnesses from among you﴾ — that is, from among the Muslims. ﴿And if they testify﴾ against them to fornication, ﴿then confine them﴾ — imprison them ﴿in houses﴾ — in prisons. This was a statement at the beginning of Islam: if the two fornicators were previously married (thayyib), they were confined and prevented from mixing with people. Then this was abrogated (nusikha) by stoning, and that is His saying: ﴿Or Allah ordains for them a way﴾, and that way is the way which Allah has ordained for them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 16:

﴿And the two of you who commit it﴾: that is, the two virgins (al-bikran) who commit fornication and engage in the indecent act. ﴿Then harm them﴾: by rebuke and reproach, which is to say, it is said to them: "You have violated the sanctities of Allah, disobeyed Him, and deserved His punishment." ﴿But if they repent﴾ from the indecent act ﴿and amend﴾ their conduct thereafter, then leave off harming them. This was at the beginning of Islam, and it was abrogated (nasakha, "repealed") by His saying: ﴿The fornicatress and the fornicator, flog each one of them﴾, to the end of the verse.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 17:

﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah﴾ That is: the repentance which Allah has obligated upon Himself, by His bounty, to accept ﴿for those who do wrong in ignorance﴾ That is: the sin of the believer is ignorance on his part, and all acts of disobedience are ignorance, and whoever disobeys his Lord is ignorant ﴿then repent soon﴾ That is: before death, even if only for the duration of a she-camel's milking interval (fuwaq naqah) ﴿then those are the ones whom Allah will turn to in forgiveness﴾ He returns to them with mercy ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ He knew what was in the hearts of the believers of affirmation, so He judged them to be repentant before death, to the measure of a she-camel's milking interval.

Translation of the passage from al-Wahidi's commentary (al-Wajiz) on Surah al-Nisa', verse 18:

﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds﴾ — that is, the polytheists and the hypocrites. ﴿Nor for those who die while they are disbelievers﴾ — meaning: there is no repentance for these people if they die upon their disbelief, because repentance is not accepted in the Hereafter. ﴿For them We have prepared﴾ — that is, We have readied and made ready.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 19:

﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you﴾ — the verse. A man, when he died, his close relative from among his paternal kin would inherit his wife and would have more right to her than anyone else. So God annulled that and informed that a man does not inherit a woman from the deceased. And His saying ﴿that you inherit women by compulsion﴾ means: inherit the women by compulsion, i.e., marry women while they are unwilling. ﴿And do not restrain them in order to take away part of what you have given them﴾ — a man would keep a woman while he had no need of her, to harm her, until she ransomed herself with her dowry, so they were forbidden from that. Then He made an exception, saying: ﴿except that they commit a clear immorality﴾, i.e., fornication. So if a man sees immorality from his wife, there is no harm in his mistreating her until she seeks khul' (divorce by ransom) from him. ﴿And live with them in kindness﴾, i.e., with what is due to them of rights, and this is before they commit immorality. ﴿And if you dislike them﴾ — the verse — i.e., in what you dislike, which is pleasing to God, there is much good and great reward, and much good in a wife you dislike is that God grants you from her a righteous child.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 20:

﴿And if you desire to replace one wife with another﴾ (the verse): that is, if a man wants to divorce his wife and marry another, it is not permissible for him to take back what he gave her as bridal payment (mahr). This is His saying: ﴿And you have given one of them a heap of gold﴾, that is, a large amount of wealth, ﴿then take not from it anything. Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?﴾, that is, by injustice ﴿and manifest sin﴾. In this there is a prohibition against harming (dirar) in other than the case of gross immorality (fahisha), namely that a husband harms his wife so that she will ransom herself from him, when she has not committed gross immorality.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 21:

﴿And how could you take it back﴾, i.e., the dowry or any part of it, ﴿when you have gone in to one another﴾, i.e., one of you has reached the other through intercourse, and it is not permissible to reclaim any part of the dowry after intercourse. ﴿And they have taken from you a solemn covenant﴾, which is what Allah has taken from men on behalf of women: to retain them with kindness or to release them with good treatment.

The Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 22:

﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married﴾ — the verse. A man among the Arabs would marry his father's wife after him, and this was a permissible marriage among the Arabs. So Allah the Exalted prohibited it and forbade it. As for His saying, ﴿except what has already passed﴾, it means: but what has already passed, for indeed Allah has pardoned it. ﴿Indeed, it﴾ — that is, that marriage ﴿was an abomination﴾ — fornication in the sight of Allah, ﴿and hatred﴾ — intense detestation, ﴿and evil was its way﴾ — and that act was ugly as a path. Then he mentioned the women who are forbidden [to marry], saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 23:

﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your paternal aunts, your maternal aunts, your brother's daughters, your sister's daughters, your mothers who have nursed you, your milk-sisters, the mothers of your wives, and your stepdaughters (raba'ib) who are in your guardianship, born of the wives with whom you have consummated the marriage;﴾ (rabA'ib) plural of rabiba, and she is the daughter of a man's wife from another husband. ﴿who are in your guardianship﴾ meaning: in your care and upbringing. ﴿And the wives of your sons﴾ and the spouses (halA'il) of ﴿your sons who are from your loins﴾, not those you have adopted. ﴿And that you should combine﴾ meaning: combining ﴿two sisters, except what has already passed﴾, what has gone before among you in the Jahiliyyah, so you will not be held accountable for it after Islam.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 24:

﴿And the married women﴾ (dhawat al-azwaj), ﴿from among women﴾, who are forbidden to everyone except their husbands, ﴿except what your right hands possess﴾ through captivity from the abode of war, for she becomes lawful to her owner after istibra' (the ascertaining that the womb is clear) by one menstrual cycle. ﴿The decree of Allah upon you﴾: He prescribed the prohibition of those women mentioned to you. ﴿And lawful for you is what is beyond that﴾, i.e., other than those women you have been told of. ﴿That you seek﴾, i.e., that you seek with your wealth, either by marriage (nikah) and a dower (sadaq), or by right of possession (milk yamin). ﴿Chaste, not debauching﴾: marrying, not committing fornication (zina). ﴿So those you enjoy from them﴾, i.e., benefit from and take pleasure in, ﴿from them﴾, that is, from women, through valid marriage, ﴿give them their wages﴾, i.e., their dowers (mahr), ﴿as an obligation﴾. If you have enjoyed her by consummation, then she is given the full dower, and if you have enjoyed her through the marriage contract alone, then she is given half the dower. ﴿And there is no blame upon you in what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾, such as reducing the dower, or releasing some or all of the marriage portion. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing﴾ of what sets right the affairs of the servants, ﴿Wise﴾ regarding what He has made clear to them of the marriage contract.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 25:

﴿And whoever among you cannot afford (ṭawl)﴾ i.e., has no means or wealth, ﴿to marry free believing women (al-muḥṣanāt)﴾ i.e., free women, ﴿then [let him marry] from what your right hands possess﴾ i.e., let him marry from what your right hands possess, meaning: a slave girl belonging to another, ﴿from your believing slave girls (fatayātikum)﴾ i.e., your female slaves. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of your faith﴾ i.e., act according to what is apparent regarding faith, for you are obligated to act upon what is manifest, while Allah takes charge of the hidden matters. ﴿You are of one another﴾ i.e., your religion is one, so you are equal in this respect; hence, whenever one of you faces necessity, it is permissible for him to marry a slave woman. ﴿So marry them with the permission of their families﴾ i.e., propose to them to their masters. ﴿And give them their bridal payments (ujūrahunna)﴾ i.e., their dowries, ﴿according to what is reasonable﴾ without delay or harm. ﴿Chaste (muḥṣanāt)﴾ i.e., modest, ﴿not fornicating openly (musāfiḥāt)﴾ i.e., not committing adultery openly, ﴿nor taking secret lovers (akhdān)﴾ i.e., committing adultery in secret. ﴿And when they are married (uḥṣina)﴾ i.e., they wed, ﴿and if they commit a grave immorality (fāḥisha)﴾ i.e., fornication, ﴿then for them is half the punishment of free chaste women (al-abkār al-ḥarā'ir)﴾ i.e., the virgin free women, ﴿of the punishment﴾ i.e., the legal penalty (ḥadd). ﴿That﴾ i.e., that marriage, the marriage of a slave woman, ﴿is for him among you who fears (khashiya) hardship (al-ʿanat)﴾ i.e., who fears that the intensity of desire might lead him to fornication, so that he would encounter hardship (al-ʿanat), i.e., the legal penalty in this world and punishment in the Hereafter. Allah permitted the marriage of a slave woman on two conditions: first, lack of means (ṭawl); second, fear of hardship (ʿanat). Then He said: ﴿And that you be patient﴾ i.e., refraining from marrying slave women ﴿is better for you﴾ so that the child does not become a slave.

Allah wants to make clear to you (ﷺ... no) — here is the translation:

﴿Allah desires to make clear to you﴾ the laws of your religion and the interests of your affairs, ﴿and to guide you to the ways of those before you﴾: the religion of Ibrahim and Isma'il, peace be upon them, which is the religion of the ḥanīfiyyah (the pure monotheistic faith), ﴿and to turn to you in forgiveness﴾: to bring you back from the disobedience in which you were to His obedience.

Allah desires to accept your repentance (﴿وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾) — that is, He brings you out of everything He dislikes to what He loves and is pleased with. (﴿وَيُرِيدُ الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الشَّهَوَاتِ﴾) — they are the fornicators and the people of falsehood in their religion — (﴿أَن تَمِيلُوا﴾) away from the truth and from the right path through disobedience (﴿مَيْلًا عَظِيمًا﴾), so that you become like them.
﴿Allah wishes to lighten for you﴾ in all the rulings of the Sharia, ﴿and man was created weak﴾, weakening him from restraint regarding women.

O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly (bil-batil), which is everything that is not permitted by the Sharia, such as usury (riba), usurpation (ghasb), gambling (qimar), theft (sariqa) and betrayal of trust (khiyana). ﴿Except that it be a transaction (tijara)﴾ — but if it is a transaction, ﴿by mutual consent among you﴾ — by the consent of the two sellers, then it is permissible. ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾ — do not let some of you kill others.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 30:

﴿And whoever does that﴾, i.e., consumes wealth falsely and kills a soul, ﴿out of transgression﴾, which is to exceed what he has been commanded, ﴿and injustice﴾, ﴿then We will drive him into a Fire﴾, i.e., We will cause him to enter a fire, ﴿and that is ever easy for Allah﴾, i.e., He is capable of that and it is not difficult for Him.

If you avoid the major sins (kaba'ir) that you are forbidden from, (kaba'ir) being every sin which Allah has concluded with a Fire, or wrath, or a curse, or a punishment, or a threat in the Qur'an, We will remove from you your bad deeds (sayyi'at), which are less than the major sins, by means of the five daily prayers, and We will admit you to a noble entrance, that is, Paradise.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 32:

﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others.﴾ [The verse]. Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, would that we were men, so that we could fight in jihad and go on military campaigns, and have a reward like the reward of men." So this verse was revealed: ﴿For men is a share of what they have earned﴾, meaning reward for [their] jihad, ﴿and for women is a share of what they have earned﴾, meaning (reward) for guarding their chastity and obeying their husbands. ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty.﴾ If you are in need of what belongs to others, then ask Allah for His bounty, and He will give you from His bounty.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 33:

﴿And for every﴾ i.e., for every person, men and women, ﴿We have appointed heirs﴾ i.e., 'asabah (agnatic relatives) and inheritors, ﴿of that which is left by parents and close relatives﴾ i.e., of those whom their parents and near relatives have left behind. That is, the 'asabah and heirs branch out from the parents and close relatives. Then he began, saying: ﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you﴾, which refers to the allies (al-hulafa'), i.e., your oaths have bound their alliance. "Aymān" is the plural of "yamin," meaning an oath. In the Jahiliyyah, a man would enter into an alliance with another man and say to him: "My blood is your blood, my war is your war, and my peace is your peace." When Islam came, it assigned to the ally a sixth share, and this is His saying: ﴿So give them their share﴾. Then this was abrogated by His saying: ﴿But blood relatives are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾, i.e., nothing of the knowledge of what He created is hidden from Him.

The commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on Surah 4, verse 34:

﴿Men are in charge of women﴾ in disciplining them, and in taking them firmly by the hand. ﴿Because Allah has favoured some of them over others﴾: men are favoured over women in knowledge, intellect, strength in conduct, fighting in the way of Allah, testimony, and inheritance. ﴿And because they spend from their wealth﴾ on them, meaning the dower (mahr) and maintenance of them. ﴿So righteous women﴾ are those women who are obedient to their husbands, which is His saying: ﴿devoutly obedient, guarding in the husband's absence what Allah has commanded them to guard﴾, meaning they guard their chastity in their husbands' absence. ﴿By what Allah has guarded﴾: by what Allah has safeguarded for them in making the dower and maintenance obligatory for them and in the husband's charge concerning them. ﴿And those [women] you fear may be rebellious﴾, meaning you know their disobedience, ﴿admonish them﴾ with the Book of Allah, and remind them of Allah and what He has commanded them. ﴿And forsake them in the beds﴾: separate yourselves from them in the beds (in the bedding). ﴿And strike them﴾ with a strike that is not severe or harsh. The husband may remedy his wife's rebellion by what Allah the Exalted has permitted: he admonishes her with his tongue; if she does not desist, he forsakes her bed; if she refuses, he strikes her; and if she refuses to be admonished by striking, the two arbitrators (al-ḥakamān, the two appointed mediators) are sent. ﴿If they obey you﴾ in what is asked of them, ﴿then do not seek a way against them﴾, meaning do not find fault with them on pretexts.

"And if you fear a breach between the two" (i.e., you know of a dispute between the spouses), "then appoint an arbiter" (ḥakaman), meaning a judge who prevents oppression, "from his family, and an arbiter from her family." They should strive and examine which of the two is the wrongdoer, then command him to return to the command of God, or separate them if they see that to be right. "If they both desire reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them," between the husband and the wife, through righteousness. "Indeed God is ever Knowing, Aware," of what is in the hearts of the spouses and the two arbiters. His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 36:

﴿And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents⦆ — ﴿وبالوالدين أحساناً﴾ means: show goodness to them both, which is righteousness (al-birr) together with gentleness of manner. ﴿And to kinsfolk﴾ — ﴿وذي القربى﴾, one who is a relative: maintain ties with him and show affection toward him. ﴿And orphans﴾ — be gentle with them and draw them near. ﴿And the needy﴾ — with a little giving or a gracious refusal. ﴿And the neighbour who is near of kin﴾ — ﴿الجار ذي القربى﴾, the one who has, along with the right of neighbourhood, the right of kinship. ﴿And the neighbour who is a stranger﴾ — ﴿الجار الجنب﴾, the one far from you in lineage. ﴿And the companion at your side﴾ — ﴿الصاحب بالجنب﴾, the fellow traveller. ﴿And the wayfarer﴾ — ﴿ابن السبيل﴾, one passing along the road (and it is said: the guest); host him and feed him until he departs. ﴿And those whom your right hands possess﴾ — namely, the slaves. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-deluded﴾ — ﴿مختالاً﴾, great in his own estimation, who does not fulfil the rights of Allah. ﴿Boastful﴾ — ﴿فخوراً﴾, over His servants, on account of the bounty that Allah has bestowed upon him from His favour.

ÿ﴿Those who are miserly﴾: that is, the Jews were stingy with their wealth, refusing to spend it in obedience to God, the Exalted. ﴿And enjoin people to be miserly﴾: they urged the Ansar not to spend their wealth on the Messenger of God (ﷺ), saying: "Indeed, we fear poverty for you." ﴿And they conceal what God has given them of His bounty﴾: that is, what is in the Torah concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his description.

﴿And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people﴾ — i.e., the hypocrites. ﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion — [then] evil is the companion he has﴾ — Satan embellishes [wrong] for him and acts upon his command. ﴿Evil is he as a companion﴾ — wretched is the companion, Satan.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 39:

﴿And what would it have harmed them﴾ That is, what would it have harmed the Jews and the hypocrites? ﴿Had they believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent from what Allah has provided them, and Allah was ever Knowing of them﴾ He would not reward them for what they spend to be seen by people.

ِ﻿Here is the translation:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong⁠ [anyone]﴾ — He does not diminish anyone's [reward] ﴿even the weight of an atom⁠﴾ — the measure of ﴿an atom⁠﴾. If it is a believer, He rewards him for it with provision in this world and reward in the Hereafter; and if it is a disbeliever, He feeds him with it in this world. ﴿And if it is a good deed⁠﴾ from a believer, ﴿He multiplies it⁠﴾ tenfold, ﴿and gives from Himself⁠﴾ — from His own presence — ﴿a great reward⁠﴾, which is Paradise.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 41:

﴿Fa-kayfa﴾ (So how?): that is, how will the condition of these Jews and hypocrites be on the Day of Resurrection? This is a rhetorical question, and its meaning is reproach. ﴿When We bring from every nation a witness﴾: that is, the prophet of every nation, who will testify against them and for them. ﴿And We bring you, O Muhammad, as a witness against these﴾: a witness against these hypocrites and polytheists, testifying to what they did.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 42:

﴿On that day﴾ i.e., on that day, ﴿those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish﴾, though they had disobeyed him in the world, ﴿that the earth were leveled over them﴾. i.e., they will become dust and level with the earth, until they and it become one single thing. ﴿And they will not be able to conceal from Allah any statement﴾, because what they did is manifest to Allah, and they will not be able to hide it.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 43:**

﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer﴾, i.e., the places of prayer, meaning the mosques, ﴿while you are intoxicated﴾. They were forbidden from prayer and from entering the mosque while in a state of intoxication (sukr). This was before the revelation of the prohibition of wine. After this verse was revealed, the Muslims would avoid intoxication and intoxicants at the times of prayer. The sakran (intoxicated person) is one whose intellect is confused, who raves, and whose speech is not consistent. Do you not see that God, exalted is He, said: ﴿until you know what you are saying﴾? So when he knows what he is saying, he is not intoxicated, and it is permissible for him to pray and enter the mosque. ﴿Nor [while you are] in a state of janabah (ritual impurity)﴾, i.e., do not approach them while you are junub (in a state of major ritual impurity), ﴿except for those passing through [as travelers]﴾, i.e., except when you pass through the mosque, entering it without staying in it, ﴿until you have washed (ightasilu)﴾ from janabah. ﴿And if you are ill﴾, i.e., an illness that harms one with water, such as sores, smallpox, and wounds, ﴿or on a journey﴾, i.e., travelling, ﴿or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself (al-ghait)﴾, i.e., or from the state of ḥadath (minor ritual impurity), ﴿or you have touched women﴾, i.e., you have touched them with your hands (lamastum, meaning touching, here understood as touching with the hands), ﴿and you find no water, then perform tayammum (dry ablution) with clean earth (ṣaʿīdan ṭayyiban)﴾, i.e., wipe yourselves with clean, fertile soil.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 44:

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book?﴾ They are the Jews. ﴿They purchase error﴾ i.e., they choose it over guidance by denying Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And they wish that you would lose the way﴾ that you, O believers, would stray from the path of guidance.

Allah knows best your enemies, so He informs you of what they are upon. ﴿And Allah is sufficient as a Protector, and Allah is sufficient as a Helper.﴾ That is: His protection and His help for you suffice you, so you have no need of anyone else, such as the Jews and those who follow their way.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 46:

﴿Among those who are Jews﴾, that is, a people ﴿who distort words from their places﴾, that is, they alter the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), his time, and his prophethood in their scripture. ﴿And they say, "We hear"﴾ your words ﴿and "We disobey"﴾ your command. ﴿And hear, but not as one who is made to hear﴾. They used to say to the Prophet (ﷺ), "Listen," and they would say to themselves, "May you not hear." ﴿And "Ra'ina," twisting their tongues﴾, that is, they say "Ra'ina" and direct it toward insulting Muhammad, peace be upon him, with foolishness (al-ru'una). We have mentioned that this was an insult in their language. ﴿And if they had said, "We hear and we obey"﴾ instead of their saying "We hear and we disobey," and they had said ﴿"Hear and look at us"﴾, that is, "look at us" in place of their saying "Ra'ina," ﴿it would have been better for them﴾ in the sight of God. ﴿But God has cursed them for their disbelief﴾, so for that reason they do not say what is better for them. ﴿So they do not believe, except a little﴾, that is, a little belief, and it is their saying: "God is our Lord, Paradise is true, and Hell is true." This little is nothing alongside their disbelief in Muhammad (ﷺ), and it is not a praise of them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 47:

﴿O you who were given the Book, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces﴾ i.e., We erase from them the eyes, mouth, nose, nostrils, and eyebrows, and make them like the hoof of a camel or like the hoof-shaped sole of a beast. ﴿And turn them back on their backs﴾ We turn them around before their faces. ﴿Or curse them﴾ or We make them apes and swine, as We did to their predecessors. ﴿And the command of Allah is ever executed﴾ there is no one who can repel His judgment or nullify His command.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 48:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾ and so on. In this verse Allah Almighty promises forgiveness for what is less than shirk (association of partners with Allah). He pardons whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, except for shirk, as a refutation of the Qadariyya (the Qadariyya, a early theological group who denied divine predestination), and this is His saying: ﴿And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾, i.e., less than shirk. ﴿And whoever associates partners with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin﴾, i.e., he has invented a sin that is not forgiven.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 49:

﴿Have you not seen those who justify themselves?﴾ That is: the Jews said, "We are the sons of God and His beloved. Whatever we do by night is expiated for us by day, and whatever we do by day is expiated for us by night." ﴿Rather, God purifies whom He wills﴾ That is: He makes whomever He wills pure, clean, and growing in righteousness, meaning: the people of monotheism (tawhid). ﴿And they will not be wronged a thread﴾ They will not be deprived of reward by the amount of a fatil, which is the thin skin that surrounds the date pit. Then He marvelled at the lie of His Prophet (ﷺ) and said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 50:

﴿Behold how they invent lies against Allah.﴾ It means: their saying, "He will expiate our sins for us." ﴿And that is sufficient as a manifest sin﴾ with their fabrication. That is, that suffices as a great (matter of) sin.

Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? (That is, the scholars of the Jews.) They believe in al-Jibt and al-Taghut (al-Jibt: the idols; al-Taghut: their custodians and interpreters). This is because they allied with the Quraysh against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and prostrated to the idols of the Quraysh, and they said to them: "You are better guided than Muhammad (peace be upon him) and more upright in way and religion." This is His saying: ﴿And they say to those who disbelieve (that is, the Quraysh): "These are better guided than those who believe in the way."﴾

Its meaning: "Or do they have a share in sovereignty?" That is, rather, do they have a share of the kingdom? He means: the Jews have no kingdom. And if they did, they would not give anyone anything, as His words state: ﴿Then they would not give the people even a speck (naqir)﴾. That is, they would be stingy even with a little. God described them with stinginess in this verse. The naqir is used as a proverb for a small thing; it is a tiny hollow in the back of a date pit, from which a date palm sprouts.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 54:

﴿Or do they envy the people﴾ meaning: Muhammad, peace be upon him, ﴿for what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾. The Jews envied Muhammad, peace be upon him, for the prophethood that Allah had given him and for the women that He had permitted him, and they said: "If he were a prophet, the matter of prophethood would have occupied him away from women." Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, We gave the family of Abraham the Book and wisdom﴾, meaning: prophethood, ﴿and We gave them a great kingdom﴾, meaning: the kingdom of David and Solomon, peace be upon them, and what they were given of women. David had ninety-nine, and Solomon had a thousand, from among free women and slave women. The meaning is: Do they envy the Prophet, peace be upon him, for prophethood and the multitude of women, when that was already granted to his family, because he is from the family of Abraham, peace be upon him?

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 55:

﴿Among them﴾ [among the People of the Book] ﴿are those who believed in him﴾ [in Muhammad, peace be upon him (ﷺ)] ﴿and among them are those who turned away from him﴾ [turned away from him and did not believe]. ﴿And Hell suffices as a blazing fire﴾ [as a punishment for those who do not believe].

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 56:

And His saying: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins⁠﻿ ... ﴾. It means: when their skins are roasted and burnt, they are renewed by being returned to the state they were in before being burnt. ﴿That they may taste the punishment⁠﻿⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿⁠⁠ ...﴾ meaning, that they may experience it and endure it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted in Might⁠﻿⁠ ...﴾ meaning, strong, unconquered by anything. ﴿Wise⁠﻿⁠ ...﴾ in what He arranges.
And His saying: ﴿And We shall admit them to shade, deep and dense﴾ — meaning: the shade of the air of Paradise, and it is ẓalīl (deep, dense), that is, lasting, which the sun does not cancel out.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 58:

﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render the trusts to their owners﴾ It was revealed concerning the returning of the key of the Ka'bah to Uthman ibn Talhah al-Hajabi (ibn Talhah al-Hajabi), when it was taken from him by force on the day of the conquest of Makkah, so Allah the Exalted commanded that it be returned to him. Then this verse is general in returning trusts to their owners, wherever they may be. ﴿Excellent is that with which He admonishes you﴾ That is: an excellent thing with which He admonishes you, namely the Qur'an. ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Hearing﴾ of your speech concerning the trust and the judgment, ﴿Seeing﴾ of what you do with it.

Abu Marzuq said: The Prophet ﷺ said to Uthman: "Give me the key." He said: "Here it is, with the trust of Allah," and handed it to him. Then he (peace be upon him) intended to give it to al-Abbas, so this verse was revealed. The Prophet ﷺ then said to Uthman: "Here, take it with the trust of Allah, eternal and everlasting, which none will take from you except a wrongdoer." Then Uthman emigrated, and he handed it to his brother Shaybah, and it remains in his descendants to this day.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 59:

﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you.﴾ They are the scholars and the jurists. It was also said: the rulers and the sultans, and obedience to them is obligatory in what agrees with the truth. ﴿And if you dispute over anything﴾ — you differ and argue, and each party says, "The statement is mine" — ﴿refer it to Allah and the Messenger﴾ — return the matter in that to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger. ﴿That is better﴾ — i.e., your referring what you differ about to the Book and the Sunnah, and your referring the arguing, ﴿and best in outcome﴾ — and most praiseworthy in consequence.

﴿Have you not seen those who claim﴾ [the verse]. A dispute arose between a Jew and a hypocrite. The Jew said, "Let Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ) judge between us." The hypocrite said, "No, rather let us have Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf judge between us." So this verse was revealed, which is His saying: ﴿They wish to take their disputes to the false deity (taghut)﴾. Its meaning: the one of transgression. ﴿And they had been commanded to reject it﴾, i.e., they were commanded not to take as allies anyone other than the people of their own religion. ﴿And Satan wishes to lead them far astray﴾, [a straying] from which they will never return to the religion of God. This is a matter of wonder for the Prophet (ﷺ) at the ignorance of the one who turns away from the judgment of God to the judgment of the taghut, while claiming that he believes in God and His Messenger.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 61:

﴿And when it is said to them﴾ i.e., to the hypocrites, ﴿"Come to what Allah has sent down"﴾ i.e., the rulings in the Qur'an, ﴿"and to the Messenger"﴾ and to the ruling of the Messenger, ﴿you see the hypocrites turning away from you, turning away∗∗﴾ they turn away from you to someone else, out of enmity toward the religion.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 62:

﴿Then how﴾, that is: how will they manage and scheme, ﴿when a disaster strikes them﴾, as a requital for them for what they have done, which is His saying: ﴿because of what their hands have sent forth﴾. The statement is complete here. Then He joined it to the meaning of what preceded, saying: ﴿Then they come to you swearing by Allah﴾, that is: they sought judgment from the tyrant (al-Taghut, a term for any object of false judgment or submission) and turned away from you, then they come to you swearing. The reason is that the hypocrites came to the Prophet ﷺ and swore that they had intended by deviating from him in the judgment nothing but reconciliation between the disputants, that is, uniting and bringing them together, and kindness through seeking a compromise in the ruling rather than pressing the bitter truth upon them. All of that was a lie on their part, because Allah the Exalted said:

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾, i.e., of polytheism and hypocrisy. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, i.e., pardon them. ﴿And admonish them﴾ with your tongue. ﴿And speak to them about themselves a far-reaching word﴾, i.e., frighten them with Allah and restrain them from what they are upon with the most eloquent restraint, so that they do not conceal their disbelief.

We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed, in what he commands and judges, not to be disobeyed and have judgment sought from other than him. And His saying, ﴿by the leave of Allah﴾, means: because Allah has permitted that and commanded obedience to him. ﴿And if they﴾, that is, the hypocrites, ﴿when they wronged themselves﴾ by seeking judgment from the disbelievers, ﴿had come to you and asked forgiveness of Allah﴾, sought refuge and repented to Allah.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 65:

And His saying: ﴿Fa-la﴾ (meaning: "No" – the matter is not as they claim, that they have believed while they oppose your judgment), ﴿wa-Rabbika la yu'minun﴾ (and by your Lord, they will not truly believe, the reality of faith) ﴿hatta yuhakkimuka fima shajara﴾ (until they make you judge in what has become disputed and confused) ﴿baynahum﴾ (among them), ﴿thumma la yajidu fi anfusihim harajan﴾ (then they find within themselves no constriction, i.e., no narrowness or doubt) ﴿mimma qadayta﴾ (regarding what you have decided, i.e., what you have made obligatory) ﴿wa-yusallimu﴾ (and submit) the matter to Allah and to His Messenger without any opposition whatsoever.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 66:

﴿And if We had decreed for them﴾, that is, for these hypocrites among the Jews, ﴿"Kill yourselves" or "Leave your homes"﴾, as We decreed that upon the Children of Israel, ﴿"Kill yourselves" or "Leave your homes"﴾, as We decreed that upon the emigrants, ﴿they would not have done it, except for a few of them﴾ because of the hardship in it, although they should have done it. ﴿And if they had done what they were being admonished﴾, that is, what they were commanded with of the rulings of the Qur'an, ﴿it would have been better for them﴾ in their livelihood and in their reward, ﴿and firmer in establishing themselves﴾ in their religion and in affirming the command of Allah.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 67:

﴿And then We would surely give them from Us a great reward﴾ means: [a reward] of the kind that none besides Us can bestow. ﴿A great reward﴾ means: Paradise.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 68:

﴿And We would have guided them﴾ — We would have shown them the way — ﴿to a straight path﴾ — to a straight religion, and it is the religion of ḥanīfiyyah (pure monotheism), not the religion of Judaism.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 69:

﴿And whoever obeys Allah﴾ [the verse]. The Muslims said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "We have you only in this world; when the Hereafter comes, you will be raised up above us, so you will be sad and we will be sad." So it was revealed: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah﴾ in the obligatory duties, ﴿and the Messenger﴾ in the sunnah, ﴿then they will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from the prophets﴾. That is: he will enjoy seeing them and visiting them, so let him not imagine that he will not see them. ﴿And the truthful ones﴾, the most excellent companions of the prophets; ﴿and the martyrs﴾, those slain in the way of Allah; ﴿and the righteous﴾, that is: the people of Paradise from among the rest of the Muslims. ﴿And excellent companions are those﴾, the prophets and these, ﴿as companions﴾, that is: friends and comrades.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 70:

﴿That﴾, i.e., that reward, which is being with the Prophets, ﴿is the bounty from Allah﴾, which He has graciously bestowed upon those who obey Him. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Knower﴾ of His creation, i.e., He is All-Knowing, nothing is hidden from Him, and no deed is lost in His sight. Then He urged His believing servants to jihad, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 71:

﴿O you who have believed, take your precaution﴾, meaning your weapons when meeting the enemy, ﴿and then go forth in multiplicity﴾, meaning, hasten forth to meet the enemy, ﴿in multiplicity﴾, meaning in separate groups, when the Messenger is not with you, ﴿or go forth all together﴾, when the Messenger goes out to jihad.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 72:

﴿And indeed among you is he who will surely lag behind﴾, i.e., he will stay back and be slow to join the jihad. They are the hypocrites, and He counted them among the believers because they displayed the word of Islam, so they entered under their rule outwardly. ﴿If a misfortune strikes you﴾ from the enemy, or hardship of livelihood, ﴿he says, "Allah has certainly blessed me﴾ by my staying behind, since I was not present, so that what has struck you does not befall me."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 73:

﴿And if a bounty from Allah should reach you﴾ — a conquest and spoils of war — ﴿he would surely say﴾ — this hypocrite, saying as one regretful and envious — ﴿"Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I could have achieved a great achievement."﴾ That is: "I would have been blessed with the same good fortune of spoils that they were blessed with." And His saying: ﴿"As if there had never been between you and him any affection"﴾ is connected in meaning to His saying: ﴿"Allah has blessed me, for I was not with them."﴾ ﴿"As if there had never been between you and him any affection"﴾ — that is: as if he had never made a pact with you regarding Islam and never supported you in fighting your enemy, and as if there had never been any affection between you and him outwardly. Then he commanded the believers to fight, saying:

Let them fight in the way of Allah those who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter, that is, for the Garden (al-Jannah), meaning they choose the Garden over remaining in this world. And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed, meaning becomes a martyr (shahid), or is victorious, meaning gains triumph, both are equal; and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And We will bestow upon him a great reward﴾, a reward without any description (limit). Then he urged the believers to strive (jihad) in His way, to rescue the weak among the believers from the hands of the polytheists, so He said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 75:

﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah and [for] the oppressed among the men, the women, and the children?﴾ They are a people in Makkah who were oppressed, so they were imprisoned and tortured. ﴿Who say, "Our Lord, bring us out﴾ to the abode of the emigration (hijrah) ﴿from this city﴾ — Makkah — ﴿whose people are oppressors﴾, i.e., they had set up partners with Allah. ﴿And appoint for us from Yourself a protector﴾, i.e., appoint over us a man from the believers who will be our ally. ﴿And appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾ who will support us against Your enemy. So Allah answered their supplication and appointed over them the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ʿAttab ibn Asid, and (Allah) aided them through him, so they became mightier through him than the oppressors before that.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 76:

﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah﴾, in obedience to Allah. ﴿And those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the Taghut﴾, i.e., in obedience to Satan. ﴿So fight against the allies of Satan﴾, the worshippers of idols. ﴿Indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak﴾, meaning: his abandonment of them on the day they were killed at Badr.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 77:

﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands"﴾ from fighting the polytheists, ﴿and establish prayer and give zakat [as] has been prescribed for you﴾. It was revealed concerning a group of believers who asked the Prophet (ﷺ) for permission to fight the polytheists while they were in Makkah, but he did not permit them. ﴿Then when fighting was prescribed for them﴾ in Madinah, ﴿behold, a party of them fear men as they should fear Allah﴾, i.e., the punishment of men by killing, ﴿or [even] greater fear﴾, i.e., more intense ﴿fear﴾. This fear was only in them by virtue of human nature, not out of aversion to Allah's command to fight. ﴿And they say﴾, out of dread of death and eagerness for life: ﴿"Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term"﴾, which is death, i.e., "If only You had left us until we die at our appointed times and spared us from being killed." ﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad: ﴿"The enjoyment of this world is little"﴾. The term of this world is near and its life is brief. ﴿And the Hereafter﴾, which is Paradise, ﴿is better for one who fears Allah﴾ and does not associate anything with Him. ﴿And you will not be wronged [even] as much as a fibre﴾, i.e., your deeds' reward will not be diminished by the amount of a date-pit's fibre. Then He informed them that their appointed terms will not miss them, even if they fortify themselves in the strongest fortresses, so He said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 78:

﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in towers built high.﴾ Fortresses and palaces, ﴿built high﴾: lofty and raised. It was also said: "towers of the sky."

﴿And if good befalls them﴾ i.e., the hypocrites and the Jews, ﴿good﴾ abundance and low prices. ﴿They say, "This is from Allah," but if evil befalls them﴾ drought and high prices, ﴿they say, "This is from you."﴾ That is, from the ill omen of Muhammad. This is because when the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Madinah and the Jews disbelieved, Allah withheld from them what He had extended to them. They said: "We have never seen anything more ill-omened than this. Since he came to us, our fruits have decreased and our prices have risen." Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "All of it"﴾ — that is, the abundance and the drought — ﴿is from Allah,﴾ from the side of Allah. ﴿So what is wrong with these people that they can hardly understand a statement?﴾ — they do not understand the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 79:

﴿Whatever good befalls you﴾, O son of Adam, ﴿of good﴾ — victory, booty, and fertility — is from the favour of God. ﴿And whatever evil befalls you﴾ — from drought, defeat, and a matter you dislike — ﴿it is from yourself﴾, that is, it is because of your sin, O son of Adam. ﴿And We have sent you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿to the people as a messenger. And sufficient is God as a witness﴾ to your message.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 80:

﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah﴾. It means: your obedience to Muhammad is obedience to Allah. ﴿But whoever turns away﴾, i.e., turns away from his obedience, ﴿We have not sent you over them as a guardian﴾, i.e., a guardian protecting them from sins, so that they do not fall into them. That is: there is no blame upon you for their turning away, because you were not sent as a guardian over them against sins.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 81:

﴿And they say﴾, i.e., the hypocrites, ﴿"Obedience"﴾, i.e., obedience to your command. ﴿But when they go out﴾ (barazu), i.e., leave ﴿from your presence, a group of them plot﴾ (bayyata), i.e., plan and conceal ﴿other than what you are told﴾ of obedience. That is, they conceal the opposite of what they display, and they plan by night what they promised you by day. ﴿But Allah records what they plot﴾, i.e., He keeps it recorded against them so that they may be recompensed for it. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, i.e., pardon them. This is because he was forbidden to kill the hypocrites at the beginning of Islam, and then that was abrogated (naskh) by His saying: ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 82:

﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ That is, the hypocrites. (Will they not) contemplate and reflect upon it? ﴿And had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction.﴾ With contradiction, falsehood, and nonsense, and variation in wording.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 83:

﴿And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear, they spread it around.﴾ It was revealed concerning the spreaders of rumours (ahl al-arajif), who were a people among the hypocrites (munafiqun) who used to spread rumours about the expeditions (sara-ya) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and would report what had befallen them before the Prophet (ﷺ) himself was informed of it. Thereby they weakened the hearts of the believers and harmed the Prophet (peace be upon him) by getting ahead of him in the reporting. And His saying: ﴿a matter of security﴾ means a report containing security, ﴿or fear﴾ means defeat. ﴿They spread it around﴾ means: they made it widely known.

﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them﴾: and if they had kept silent about it until the Messenger himself was the one to make it known, and those in authority, such as Abu Bakr, Umar and Ali, may Allah be pleased with them. It was also said: the commanders of the expeditions. ﴿those of them who investigate it would have known it﴾: those who follow it and seek knowledge of that matter ﴿from among them﴾, from the Messenger and those in authority. ﴿And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you﴾, that is, Islam, ﴿and His mercy﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿you would have followed Satan, except for a few﴾ of those whom Allah protected, such as those who were guided by their own intellects to abandon the worship of idols without a messenger or a scripture, like Zayd ibn Amr, Waraqa ibn Nawfal and the seekers of religion. This is a reminder to the believers of Allah's blessing upon them, by which they were saved from hypocrisy and from that for which the hypocrites were censured.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 84:

﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself.﴾ That is, except the action of yourself, meaning: there is no harm upon you in the action of others, so do not concern yourself with the staying behind of those who stay back from jihad. ﴿And urge the believers﴾ — urge them to fight. ﴿Perhaps Allah﴾ — "perhaps" here is a binding affirmation from Allah — ﴿will restrain﴾ — will turn away and prevent — ﴿the might of those who disbelieve﴾ — their severity and their power. ﴿And Allah is stronger in might﴾ — in punishment — ﴿and stronger in exemplary punishment﴾ — in retribution.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 85:

﴿Whoever intercedes for a good cause﴾: this is every intercession that is permissible in the religion. ﴿He will have a share in it﴾: he will have a reward for it. ﴿And whoever intercedes for an evil cause﴾: that is, what is not permissible in the religion to intercede for. ﴿He will have a portion of it﴾: that is, a share of the burden and sin. ﴿And Allah is ever Muqit over all things﴾: that is, Capable (muqtadir).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 86:

﴿And when you are greeted with a greeting﴾, that is: when peace is extended to you with a salutation, ﴿then greet with better than it﴾, that is: respond with an addition to the greeting if the one greeting you is from among the people of Islam, ﴿or return it﴾ if he is from among the People of the Book (so say: "Wa 'alaykum," and do not add to that). ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, a Reckoner﴾ (Ḥafīẓan, i.e., Watchful), who will call to account.

Allah—there is no god but Him. He will surely gather you ﴿Allah—there is no god but Him. He will surely gather you﴾ That is: by Allah, He will surely gather you in the graves ﴿until the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt﴾ — no doubt about it. ﴿And who is more truthful in statement than Allah?﴾ That is: in speech and report, meaning: there is no breaking of His promise.

Correction to the above: the full, accurate rendering is as follows.

Allah—there is no god but Him. He will surely gather you ("by Allah, He will surely gather you in the graves") until the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And who is more truthful in statement than Allah? That is: in speech and report; meaning, there is no breaking of His promise.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 88:

﴿So what is wrong with you that you have become two factions regarding the hypocrites?﴾ It was revealed concerning a people who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina and stayed as long as Allah willed. Then they said: "We have found Medina unhealthy (ijtawaynā al-madīnah)," so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave them permission to leave. When they left, they kept travelling stage by stage until they joined the polytheists. The believers disagreed about them. Some of them said: "They are disbelievers who have apostatised." Others said: "They are Muslims until you know that they have changed." So Allah clarified their disbelief in this verse. The meaning is: What is wrong with you, disagreeing about these hypocrites, becoming two factions, two groups? ﴿And Allah has reverted them (arkasahum)﴾ He returned them to the ruling of the disbelievers, of humiliation, abasement, captivity and killing. ﴿Because of what they earned﴾ because of what they displayed of apostasy after they had been upon hypocrisy. ﴿Do you wish﴾ O believers ﴿to guide﴾ i.e., to set right ﴿those whom Allah has sent astray﴾ whom Allah has not guided; i.e., you say: "These are rightly guided," while Allah has already sent them astray. ﴿And whoever Allah sends astray, you will never find for him a way﴾ i.e., a religion or path, or a route to proof.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 89:

﴿They wish﴾ i.e., these people (wadda) ﴿that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved, and that you would be equal﴾ — you and they — ﴿so do not take from among them allies﴾, i.e., do not make them your allies (tuwalluhum) nor have inner friendship with them (tubatinuhum), ﴿until they emigrate in the way of Allah﴾, until they return to the Messenger of Allah. ﴿But if they turn away﴾ from emigration and persist in what they are upon, ﴿then seize them﴾ by taking them captive. ﴿And do not take from among them a protector or a helper﴾, i.e., do not make them your protectors (la tatawallawhum) nor seek their help against your enemy.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 90:

﴿Except those who seek refuge⁠⁠ —﴾ meaning: kill them wherever you find them, except those who join and take refuge ﴿with a people between whom and you there is a covenant﴾, so that they enter among them by alliance and protection, ﴿or who come to you with hearts constricted⁠⁠﴾, meaning: or who join a people who came to you while their hearts were constricted from fighting you. They were the Banu Mudlij, who were at peace with the Prophet ﷺ. This is an explanation that whoever joins a people who have a covenant with the Prophet ﷺ has the same ruling as them regarding the sparing of blood and property. Then all of this was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of the sword. Then Allah, exalted is He, mentioned His favour in restraining the might of the covenant-holders, and said: ﴿And had Allah willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you⁠⁠﴾, meaning: if their hearts were constricted from fighting them, that is only because Allah, exalted is He, cast terror into their hearts; and had Allah strengthened their hearts to fight you, they would have fought you. ﴿So if they keep away from you⁠⁠﴾, meaning: in war, ﴿and offer you peace⁠⁠﴾, meaning: reconciliation, ﴿then Allah has not made for you any way⁠⁠﴾ against them, in fighting them or shedding their blood. Then He commanded them to fight those who were not on the path of these people, and said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 91:

﴿You will find others﴾ — the verse. These are a people who used to show agreement with their kin among the disbelievers, while showing Islam to the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers, desiring by this safety from both sides. So Allah informed His Prophet (peace be upon him) of their hypocrisy. This is His saying: ﴿They wish to be secure from you and to be secure from their own people.﴾ And His saying: ﴿Every time they are sent back to temptation (al-fitnah), they are plunged back into it.﴾ Whenever they are called to polytheism (shirk), they return to it. ﴿And those — We have given you clear authority over them.﴾ That is: a clear proof (hujjah) for fighting them, because they are treacherous and do not keep their covenant with you.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 92:

﴿And it is not for a believer to kill a believer﴾ at all, ﴿except by mistake﴾. Except that a believer may err in killing. ﴿And whoever kills a believer by mistake﴾, such as one who aims his shot at someone else and hits him, ﴿then [he must free] a believing slave and pay blood-money (diyah) delivered to his family﴾, to all his heirs. ﴿Unless they forgo it﴾, meaning they pardon and waive the blood-money. ﴿But if [the slain] was from a people﴾ at war with you, ﴿and he was a believer﴾, ﴿then [the penance is] freeing a believing slave﴾ as expiation for the killing, and there is no blood-money, because his kinsmen and family are disbelievers, so they do not inherit his blood-money. ﴿And if he was from a people between you and them is a covenant﴾, such as the people of dhimmah (protected non-Muslims), then blood-money and expiation are obligatory for him. ﴿But whoever does not find﴾ a slave to free, ﴿then [he must fast] two consecutive months as a repentance from Allah﴾, meaning that Allah accepts the repentance of the killer, since he did not investigate the slain man's condition, and since he did not exert himself to avoid error.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 93:

﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ and so on. God has made the threat against one who intentionally kills a believer severe, in order to emphasize the deterrent and the restraint.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 94:

﴿O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of Allah, investigate carefully﴾ — that is, when you travel through the land, ﴿investigate carefully﴾, that is, take your time and be certain.

It was revealed concerning a man who had withdrawn with a flock of sheep of his to a mountain, and he met a detachment (sariyyah) of the Muslims, among whom was Usamah ibn Zayd. He came to them and said: "Peace be upon you; there is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." He had accepted Islam, but Usamah killed him and they seized his sheep. So it was revealed as a prohibition against shedding the blood of one who is in such a state. Usamah had said: "He only said it seeking refuge." Then Allah said: ﴿And do not say to one who gives you [the greeting of] peace, "You are not a believer," seeking the goods of worldly life﴾ — that is, who greets you with this greeting — ﴿for with Allah are many spoils﴾, meaning: great reward for one who refrains from killing one who has offered you peace. ﴿Thus were you before⁠﻿⁠ — unbelievers and astray, just as this slain man was before his Islam; then Allah bestowed His favor upon you with Islam, just as He bestowed His favor upon the slain man. That is, every one of those who accepted Islam from among the disbelievers is in the position of this one who sought refuge in Islam: the outward profession of Islam is accepted from him. Then He repeated the command to investigate, saying: ﴿So investigate carefully. Indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾ — that is, He knows that you killed him for his property.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent his blood-money (diyah) to his family, returned his sheep to them, sought forgiveness for Usamah, and ordered him to free a slave.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 95:

﴿Those believers who sit at home, other than those who have a harm (or disability), are not equal﴾. That is: the healthy ones who have no illness that harms them and prevents them from jihad, these are not equal. ﴿And those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives﴾ ﴿Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit at home﴾ from among those with an excuse, ﴿by a degree﴾, because the strivers actually carried out the obedience, while those who sat at home with an excuse only intended it. Even though they were in resolve and intention on striving, actually performing the act of obedience is above merely intending it through one's intention. ﴿And to each﴾ of the strivers and of those who sat at home with a valid excuse, ﴿Allah has promised the best reward﴾, meaning Paradise. ﴿And Allah has preferred the strivers over those who sit at home﴾ without an excuse, ﴿with a great reward﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 96:

﴿Degrees from Him﴾: that is, ranks, some of them above others, from the ranks of honor.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 97:

﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death﴾, that is, whose souls are seized. It was revealed concerning a people who had embraced Islam but had not emigrated, until the polytheists went out to Badr and they went out with them, and they were killed on the day of Badr. The angels struck their faces and their backs. As for His saying, ﴿wronging themselves﴾, [this refers to] their remaining in the abode of polytheism and their going out with the polytheists to fight the Muslims. ﴿The angels said, "In what [condition] were you?"﴾, that is, the angels said to them, as a question of rebuke and reproach: "Were you among the polytheists or among the Muslims?" They excused themselves by weakness in resisting the people of polytheism in their own land, so ﴿they said, "We were oppressed in the land"﴾, that is, in Makkah. So the angels argued with them concerning emigration to a land other than their own, and ﴿they [the angels] said, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious, so that you could have emigrated therein?" Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾. Allah the Exalted informed that these people are among the people of the Fire. Then He made an exception for those who were truthful that they were indeed oppressed, saying:

Except the oppressed (al-mustad'afin), i.e., those who are found to be weak, ﴿who are unable to devise a plan﴾, meaning they have no ability to find a way out, nor provision, nor strength to leave, ﴿and do not know the way﴾, meaning they do not know a path to Medina.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 100:

﴿And whoever emigrates in the way of Allah will find in the earth many a refuge and abundance﴾. That is: one who emigrates (muhajiran) and changes his place (mutahawwilan), ﴿many a refuge and abundance﴾ in provision.

﴿And whoever leaves his home emigrating to Allah…﴾ The verse was revealed concerning Habib ibn Damrah al-Laythi, who was an elderly old man. He set out heading toward Madinah and died on the way. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had he reached Madinah, he would have had a more complete reward." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, and informed that whoever intends an act of obedience and then is prevented by an excuse from completing it, Allah records for him the reward of the complete act of obedience. The meaning of ﴿his reward has fallen upon Allah﴾ is that it became obligatory by His making it obligatory.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 101:

﴿And when you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer﴾. The verse was revealed concerning the permission to shorten the prayer (qasr al-salah) during travel. The apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that shortening the prayer is permitted by travel and by fear, due to His saying: ﴿If you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you﴾, meaning: will kill you. The consensus (ijma') is established that shortening the prayer is permissible during travel without fear, and the Sunnah has been established on this from the Prophet (ﷺ). But mention of fear in the verse was made in reference to the circumstances that were most common in their journeys at that time. Then he mentioned the prayer of fear, saying:

﴿And when you [O Prophet] are among them﴾ i.e., when you, O Prophet, are with the believers in their military campaigns and in their fear, ﴿and establish prayer for them﴾ i.e., you begin it leading them, ﴿let a group of them stand with you﴾ — half of them pray with you, ﴿and let them take their weapons﴾ i.e., let the rest take their weapons, ﴿and when they have prostrated﴾ — when the group that stood with you has prostrated, ﴿let them be behind you﴾ i.e., those who were ordered to take up arms, ﴿and let another group come forward﴾ i.e., those who were behind them guarding them, ﴿who have not prayed﴾ (with you the first rak'ah), ﴿and let them pray with you﴾ (the second rak'ah), ﴿and let them take their precaution﴾ (against their enemy), ﴿and their weapons﴾ (their weapons being with them) — meaning: those who prayed the first time. ﴿The disbelievers wish that you would be negligent of your weapons and your belongings﴾ during your prayer, ﴿so they could attack you in one assault﴾ with fighting. ﴿And there is no blame upon you if you put down your weapons, if you have discomfort from rain or are ill﴾ — a concession to them to leave off carrying weapons during prayer; carrying them is obligatory according to some and a emphasized sunnah according to others, so God granted them leave to omit it for the excuse of rain and illness, because weapons burden the sick and are spoiled by rain. ﴿And take your precaution﴾ i.e., be on guard during prayer so that the enemy does not catch you off guard.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 103:

﴿So when you have completed the prayer﴾, that is, finished the prayer of fear, ﴿remember Allah﴾ by affirming His oneness and giving Him thanks in all your circumstances, ﴿and when you are secure﴾, that is, you have returned to your families and settled, ﴿then establish the prayer﴾, that is, complete it. ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times﴾, that is, obligatory and prescribed at fixed times.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 104:

﴿And do not weaken﴾ i.e., do not become feeble ﴿in pursuit of the people﴾, meaning Abu Sufyan and those with him, when they withdrew from Uhud. God the Exalted commanded His Prophet to pursue them in their tracks a few days after the battle. His companions complained of the wounds they had suffered, so God the Exalted said: ﴿If you suffer pain, then they too suffer pain as you suffer pain﴾, i.e., if you are in pain from your wounds, they too are in a state like yours of the pain of wounds. ﴿But you hope from God﴾ for God's help to you and the manifestation of your religion (in this world) and His reward in the next ﴿that they do not hope for﴾. ﴿And God was ever Knowing﴾ of His creation ﴿Wise﴾ in what He decrees.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 105:

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾. This verse and what follows was revealed concerning the story of Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq, who stole a coat of mail and then threw it at a Jew. When the coat of mail was demanded from him, he shifted the blame onto the Jew and accused him of the theft. The people of Tu'mah and the people of the Jew gathered and came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The people of Tu'mah asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to argue on behalf of their companion and to clear him, saying: "If you do not do so, our companion will be disgraced and the Jew will be cleared." The Prophet (ﷺ) almost resolved to do so, and then the saying of Allah, the Exalted, was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾, meaning in judgment, not in transgressing within it, ﴿so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, that is, by what Allah has taught you, ﴿and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾, namely Tu'mah and his people, ﴿an advocate﴾, meaning one who disputes on their behalf.
{Wa-staghfir Allah} — seek forgiveness of Allah for your arguing on behalf of Ṭu'me and your intention to cut off (the hand of) the Jew.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 107:

﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves.﴾ They betray themselves by disobedience, because the bearing of their betrayal returns upon them. He means: Ta'mah and his people. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is habitually treacherous and sinful.﴾ That is, Ta'mah, because he betrayed (in the matter of) the coat of mail, and sinned in his accusing the Jew.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 108:

﴿They hide [themselves] from the people, yet they cannot hide [themselves] from Allah, and He is with them﴾ — He has knowledge of what they conceal — ﴿when they plot by night what He does not approve of in speech﴾ — they prepare and devise at night — and that is that Ta'mah said: "I will accuse the Jew of being the thief of the coat of mail, and I will swear that I did not steal, so his oath will be accepted, because I am upon their religion." ﴿And Allah is ever, of what they do, All-Encompassing﴾ — Knowing. Then He addressed the people of Ta'mah, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 109:

﴿Ha antum ha'ulai jadaltum﴾ (Here you are, you argued) khasamtum (you disputed) ﴿on their behalf﴾ on behalf of Tu'mah and his kin ﴿in the life of this world. But who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection﴾ i.e., no one does that, and on that Day there will be no guardian (wakil) for them to take up their affairs and dispute on their behalf. Then he offered repentance to Tu'mah and his people with His words:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 110:

﴿And whoever does wrong﴾, an act of disobedience, as the people of Ṭu'mah did, ﴿or wrongs himself﴾ by a sin, like the deed of Ṭu'mah, ﴿then seeks forgiveness from Allah﴾, the verse… Then he mentioned that the harm of disobedience falls only upon the disobedient one, and does not reach Allah from His disobedience with any harm, so He said:
﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself; and Allah is ever All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ — about the thief. ﴿All-Wise﴾: He ruled for the amputation (of the hand) against Ṭu'ma.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 112:

﴿And whoever earns a sin﴾, a sin between himself and Allah the Exalted, i.e., his false oath that he did not steal, ﴿or a sin﴾, a sin between himself and the people, i.e., his theft, ﴿then throws it upon an innocent person﴾, i.e., with his sin, ﴿innocent﴾, as Ṭu'mah did when he accused the Jew of theft, ﴿then he has borne a slander﴾ by accusing the innocent, ﴿and a manifest sin﴾ through the false oath and the theft.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 113:

﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾ — through prophethood and protection from error — ﴿a group of them would have resolved﴾ — indeed, they resolved — ﴿to mislead you﴾ — from among the people of Ṭu'mah — ﴿to mislead you﴾, that is: to make you err in judgment. This is because they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to argue on their behalf and to rule against the Jew. ﴿But they do not mislead except themselves﴾ — through their cooperation in sin and transgression and their giving of false witness and slander. ﴿And they do not harm you in anything﴾, because the harm falls upon the one who testifies falsely. Then Allah bestowed His favour upon him and said: ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾, that is: judgment by revelation, and He made clear to you what contains wisdom.
