So when it became evident that the thief was Ṭu'mah, his people conferred together concerning his affair, and Allah the Exalted sent down:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 114:

﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk﴾, i.e., their confidential conversations [*najwā*]. ﴿Except for one who enjoins﴾, i.e., except in the secret talk of one who enjoins ﴿charity﴾. Mujahid said: this verse is general for people, meaning that there is no good in what people confide in one another and engage in as talk, except what is among the acts of righteousness. Then he clarified that this only benefits the one who seeks thereby what is with God, so He said: ﴿And whoever does that﴾ [to the end of the verse]. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ruled against Ṭu'mah with amputation, so he feared disgrace for himself, fled to Makkah, and joined the polytheists. Then there was revealed his saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 115:

﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him﴾ — that is, contradicts him — ﴿after guidance has become clear to him﴾ — faith in Allah and His Messenger. This was because the verse had made clear what was needed for the message, by what Allah, glorified is He, had made known of his affair; so he showed enmity to the Prophet ﷺ after the proof had become evident and the evidence had been established. ﴿And follows other than the way of the believers﴾ — other than the religion of those who affirm the oneness of Allah — ﴿We will leave him to what he has turned to﴾ — we will abandon him to what he has chosen for himself — ﴿and burn him in Hell﴾ — we will cause him to enter it and bind him to the Fire. Then he associated others with Allah (Tu'mah), and he was worshipping an idol until he died, so Allah revealed concerning him:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 123:

﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book﴾. It was revealed concerning the disbelievers of Quraysh and the Jews. Then he explained the virtue of the believers over others with His saying:
﴿And whoever does righteous deeds﴾, the verse... and with His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 125:

﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits himself entirely to Allah⁠ — ﴾ that is, who directs his worship to Allah, humbling himself before Him ﴿while he is a doer of good⁠﴾ — monotheist ﴿and follows the religion of Ibrahim, inclining toward truth⁠﴾ — the religion of Ibrahim is included in the religion of Muhammad, peace be upon them both. So whoever affirms the religion of Muhammad has followed the religion of Ibrahim, peace be upon him ﴿And Allah took Ibrahim as a khalil⁠﴾ — chosen friend, distinguished by the message and prophethood, loving him with pure love.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 127:

﴿They ask you for a ruling⁠﴾ — they seek from you a fatwa (legal verdict) ﴿concerning women﴾ — concerning their inheritance. The Arabs did not give women or children any share of the inheritance. ﴿Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also] what is recited to you⁠﴾ — that is, the Qur'an also gives you a ruling, meaning the verse on inheritance at the beginning of this surah ﴿concerning⁠﴾ the inheritance of ﴿orphaned women⁠﴾, because it was revealed regarding the case of Umm Kujjah, who had daughters. ﴿To whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them⁠﴾ — that is, what has been obligated for them of the inheritance. ﴿And you desire⁠﴾ to refrain from ﴿marrying them⁠﴾ because of their plainness. ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: It was revealed concerning the orphan girl whose guardian is averse to marrying her and does not marry her, and so he prevents her [from marrying others] out of greed for her inheritance, and so he was forbidden from that. ﴿And [concerning] the oppressed among the children⁠﴾ — that is, He gives you a ruling concerning the young boys and girls, that you should give them their rights. ﴿And that you should stand⁠﴾ — that is, and concerning that you should stand ﴿for orphans with justice⁠﴾ — that is, with fairness in their dowries and their inheritances. ﴿And whatever good you do⁠﴾ — of goodness in what I have commanded you ﴿indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of it⁠﴾ — He will reward you for it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 128:

﴿And if a woman fears﴾ knows ﴿from her husband﴾ her husband ﴿ill-treatment (nushuz)﴾ haughtiness toward her out of dislike for her, which is that he abandons intercourse with her, ﴿or aversion (i'rad)﴾ by turning his face away from her, ﴿then there is no blame upon them both if they make a settlement between themselves, a settlement﴾ concerning the division (of nights) and maintenance, and it is that she agrees to less than her right, or forgoes some of her dower so that the husband will treat her equally with her co-wife in the division. This is when she agrees to that out of dislike of separation from her husband, and she is not to be compelled to this, because if she does not agree to less than her right, then it is obligatory upon the husband to give her her right of maintenance and of spending the night. ﴿And settlement is better﴾ than ill-treatment and aversion, meaning: if they reach an agreement on something, it is better than that they persist in ill-treatment and mutual resentment. ﴿And souls are present with stinginess﴾ meaning: the woman is stingy with her share of her husband, and the man is stingy toward the woman with himself when another woman is more beloved to him than she is. ﴿And if you do good﴾ in companionship and association ﴿and fear God﴾ from injustice and partiality, ﴿then indeed God is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾, nothing is lost to Him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 129:

﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you are eager [to do so]﴾: you will not be able to achieve equality between them in love, even if you strive. ﴿So do not incline completely [away from one]﴾: toward the one you love, in provision and in the division [of nights]. ﴿And leave her as if suspended﴾: so that you leave the other as though she were hanging, neither a widow nor one who has a husband. ﴿And if you reconcile﴾: by justice in the division [of nights]. ﴿And fear [Allah]﴾: from tyranny. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾: for what you feel inclined toward the one you love in your heart. And when he mentioned the permissibility of reconciliation between them, if they both wish to remain together, he then mentioned separation after it, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 130:

﴿And if they separate﴾ That is: if the older wife refuses reconciliation and insists only on equal treatment between herself and the younger one, and they part by divorce, then Allah has promised both of them that He will enrich each of them from His abundant bounty after the divorce, by His saying: ﴿And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance, and Allah is ever All-Encompassing, All-Wise﴾ [an-Nisa 4:130]. Wasi'an (All-Encompassing) means for all His creatures in provision and bounty. ﴿Hakiman﴾ (All-Wise) means in what He decrees and admonishes.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 133:

﴿If He wills, He will take you away, O people,﴾ meaning: the polytheists and the hypocrites. ﴿And bring others﴾ better than you and more obedient to God.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 134:

﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world﴾, that is, its benefits. ﴿Then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾, that is, the good of this world and the Hereafter is with Him, so let him seek it from Him. This is an allusion (ta'ridh) to the disbelievers, who did not believe in the Resurrection and used to say: ﴿Our Lord, give us in this world,﴾ and ﴿they have no share in the Hereafter.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 135:

﴿O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice﴾ standing firm in justice, ﴿witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives.﴾ That is: bear witness for Allah with the truth, even if the truth is against the witness himself, or against his parents or relatives. ﴿Whether he be rich or poor﴾ the one testified against, ﴿so do not favor the rich for his wealth, nor be unfair to the poor for his poverty.﴾ ﴿And Allah is more worthy of both.﴾ That is: more knowing of them than you, because He is in charge of knowing their circumstances. ﴿So do not follow [your] desire﴾ in testimony, and fear [Allah]. ﴿Lest you deviate﴾ That is: incline and act unjustly. ﴿And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it]﴾ That is: you evade the testimony, and conceal and deny it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted.﴾ So He will reward the doer of good according to his good and the doer of evil according to his evil.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 136:

﴿O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾ That is: remain steadfast in faith. ﴿And the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger﴾ the Qur'an. ﴿And the Book which He sent down before﴾ That is: every book that was sent down upon a prophet before the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 137:

﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾, that is, the Jews who believed in the Torah, ﴿then disbelieved﴾ by opposing it, ﴿then believed﴾ in the Gospel, ﴿then disbelieved﴾ by opposing it, ﴿then increased in disbelief﴾ by [rejecting] Muhammad, ﴿Allah would not forgive them﴾ as long as they persisted in what they were upon, ﴿nor would He guide them to a path﴾ of guidance. Then He joined the hypocrites with them, because they used to take them as allies, so He said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 139:

﴿Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers.﴾ This verse describes the hypocrites. They would ally themselves with the Jews, opposing the Muslims, imagining that they had strength and protection. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿Do they seek honour with them? Indeed, honour is wholly with God.﴾ That is, the strength of prevailing over Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Indeed, honour﴾ means victory and strength, ﴿is wholly with God.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 140:

﴿And it has already been revealed to you﴾ O believers, ﴿in the Book﴾ in the Qur'an, ﴿that when you hear the disbelief in the signs of Allah and their mockery, ﴾ then do not sit with them until they engage in talk﴾ other than disbelief and mockery. That is, His saying in Surat al-An'am: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs﴾ This was among what was revealed to them in the Book. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, you would then be like them.﴾ That is: if you sit with them, content with what they do of disbelief in the Qur'an and mockery of it. This is because the hypocrites used to sit with the rabbis of the Jews and mock the Qur'an, so Allah, glorified is He, forbade the Muslims from sitting with them. ﴿Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell all together﴾ He means: just as they gathered in mockery of the signs, they will gather in Hell for punishment.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 141:

﴿Those who wait and watch over you﴾ means: the hypocrites, who wait for misfortunes to befall you. ﴿If you achieve a victory from God﴾ means dominance over the Jews. ﴿They say: "Were we not with you?"﴾ so give us a share of the spoils. ﴿And if the disbelievers have a share﴾ of success against the Muslims, ﴿they say﴾ to them, ﴿"Did we not gain mastery over you"﴾ meaning, overpower you, ﴿"and protect you from the believers"﴾ by discouraging them from you and by informing you of their affairs through our correspondence with you. ﴿God will judge between you﴾ meaning, between the believers and the hypocrites, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾ meaning, He has delayed their punishment until that Day and lifted the sword from them (in this world). ﴿And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾ meaning: a proof on the Day of Resurrection, because He will single out the believers for bliss, and the disbelievers will not share with them in the honours that they receive, unlike in this world.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 142:

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites try to deceive Allah﴾, that is: they act like one who deceives, by showing what they display and concealing the opposite. ﴿But He is the One who deceives them﴾, meaning He will requite them for their deception. This is because they are given light just as the believers are given light; but when they go on a little, their light is extinguished and they remain in darkness. ﴿And when they stand up for prayer﴾ with the people, ﴿they stand up lazily﴾, reluctantly, ﴿showing off to the people﴾, so that the people will see it, not in obedience to the command of Allah; meaning, so that the people see them praying while not intending the Face of Allah. ﴿And they do not remember Allah except a little﴾, because they perform it out of showing off and reputation; and if they had intended by it the Face of Allah, it would have been much.

﴿Wavering between that﴾: vacillating between disbelief and faith, neither sincere believers nor openly associators who declare their polytheism. ﴿Neither to these nor to those﴾: neither of the Ansar (the Helpers of Madinah) nor of the Jews. ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, you will never find for him a way﴾: whomever Allah misguides, you will never find for him a religion.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 144:

﴿O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers﴾ meaning: the Ansar. He says: do not take as allies the Jews of Qurayzah and al-Nadir. ﴿Do you wish to give Allah against yourselves a clear authority?﴾ a clear proof against your punishment for your alliance with the Jews. That is: if you do that, the proof will be against you for punishment.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 145:

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire﴾, i.e., in the lowest of the levels (darajat) of the Fire. ﴿And you will not find for them a helper﴾, a protector who would shield them from the punishment of Allah.

﴿Except those who repent﴾ from hypocrisy, ﴿and amend﴾ their deeds, ﴿and hold fast to Allah﴾ , that is, they seek refuge in Him, ﴿and make their religion sincere for Allah﴾ from any admixture of showing-off (riya'), ﴿then those are with the believers﴾ . That is: they will be in a position closer to them after all this. Then He placed the reward of the believers in the future tense, because they are joined to them, so He said: ﴿And Allah will soon give the believers a great reward﴾.

﴿What would Allah do with your punishment﴾ with the punishment of His creation, ﴿if you are grateful﴾ acknowledge His favor, ﴿and believe﴾ in His Prophet. ﴿And Allah was ever Appreciative﴾ of the little of your deeds, ﴿Knowing﴾ of your intentions.

Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech (Allah does not love ﴿the public mention of evil in speech﴾). It was revealed as a concession (rukhsah) to the wronged person, that he may openly complain of the wrongdoer. The reason: a guest came down upon a people, and they treated his hospitality badly, so he complained about them, and this verse was revealed as a concession for him to complain.

As for His words ﴿except one who has been wronged﴾: but the one who has been wronged may openly speak of evil in speech, and that is permitted to him. ﴿And Allah is ever Hearing﴾ of the words of the wronged, ﴿Knowing﴾ of what he conceals. That is: let him speak the truth and not exceed what he has been permitted to say.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 149:

﴿If you show good⁠ — from acts of righteousness — ﴿or conceal it, or pardon an evil⁠ — that comes to you from your Muslim brother — ﴿indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning, [and] Competent⁠ — over His reward﴾ for the one who pardons.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 150:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers﴾ are the Jews, who disbelieved in ʿIsa (ʿalayhi as-salam) and the Injil, and in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an. ﴿And they wish to make distinction between Allah and His messengers﴾ by believing in Allah and disbelieving in the messengers. ﴿And they say, "We believe in some"﴾ of the messengers ﴿"and disbelieve in others"﴾ of them. ﴿And they wish to adopt between that a way﴾ between belief in some and disbelief in others, a religion they follow.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 151:

﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth.﴾ That is: their believing in some of the messengers does not remove from them the name of disbelief. Then it was revealed concerning the believers.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 153:

﴿They ask you, the People of the Book, [to bring down a book to them from the heaven]﴾. The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he bring them a book all at once from the heaven, as Moses had brought one. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. And His saying: ﴿So they had asked Moses for greater than that﴾ means: the seventy [men] who are mentioned in His saying: ﴿And when you said, "O Moses, we will never believe you"﴾ ﴿Then you took the calf [for worship]﴾ means: those whom Moses left behind with Aaron ﴿after clear proofs had come to them﴾: the staff, the hand, and the splitting of the sea. ﴿Then We pardoned you for that﴾: We did not eradicate the calf-worshippers. ﴿And We gave Moses clear authority﴾: a manifest proof with which he prevailed over those who opposed him.

ورفعنا فوقهم الطور ﴿And We raised over them the mountain (Tur)﴾ when they refused to accept the law of the Torah. ﴿By their covenant﴾, i.e., by taking their covenant. ﴿And We said to them, "Do not transgress in the Sabbath"﴾, i.e., do not transgress by hunting fish on it. ﴿And We took from them a solemn covenant﴾, a firm pledge concerning the Prophet ﷺ.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 155:

﴿Fa-bi-mā naqḍihim mīthāqahum﴾ (So because of their breaking their covenant). That is: "fa-bi-naqḍihim" (because of their breaking), and "mā" here is superfluous (zā'idah), for emphasis (li-l-ta'kīd). His saying ﴿Bal ṭaba'a Allāhu 'alayhā bi-kufrihim﴾ (Nay, Allah has sealed over them because of their disbelief) means: Allah set a seal upon their hearts, so they do not comprehend admonition, as a recompense to them for their disbelief. ﴿Fa-lā yu'minūna illā qalīlan﴾ (so they do not believe, except a few) means: those who believed.
﴿And for their disbelief﴾ in the Messiah, ﴿and for their saying against Maryam a tremendous slander﴾ when they accused her of fornication.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 157:

﴿And their saying, "Indeed, we killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah." And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear to them so.﴾ That is: the likeness of Jesus was cast upon another for them, until they thought, when they saw him, that he was the Messiah. ﴿And indeed, those who differed concerning him﴾ That is: concerning his killing. That was because when they killed the person who had been made to resemble him, the likeness had been cast upon his face while the body was not given the likeness of Jesus's body. So when they killed him and looked at him, they said: "The face is the face of Jesus, but the body is the body of someone else." Thus they differed: some of them said, "This is Jesus," and some of them said, "This is not Jesus." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿they are in doubt about it﴾ That is: about his killing. ﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾ of Jesus, ﴿whether he was killed or not﴾, ﴿except the following of conjecture﴾ but they follow conjecture. ﴿And they did not kill him for certain﴾ and they did not kill the Messiah with certainty that he was the Messiah.

﴿Bal rafa'ahu Allah ilayh﴾ (Nay, God raised him up to Himself). That is, to the place where no judgment applies to anyone other than God. His being raised to that place was a raising to Him, because he was lifted above having the judgment of any of the servants applied to him. ﴿Wa kana Allah 'Azizan﴾ (And God is Almighty) in His power to save whomever He wills of His servants; ﴿Hakiman﴾ (All-Wise) in His management of the salvation.

And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in him (before his death). That is: none of the People of the Scripture will fail to believe in Jesus ﴿before his death﴾, when he sees the angel; and his faith will not benefit him at that time. No Jew dies until he believes in Jesus.

﴿And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾, that he (Jesus) had conveyed the message and acknowledged servitude for himself.

﴿So for the wrongdoing of those who were Jews﴾: God punished the Jews for their wrongdoing and transgression by forbidding them certain things, which are what is mentioned in His saying: ﴿And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws﴾. Then He excepted their believers, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 162:

﴿But those firm in knowledge﴾ means: those who are thorough in the knowledge of the Book among them, such as ʿAbdullah ibn Salam and his companions, ﴿and the believers﴾ from among the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿who believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and the establishers of prayer and the givers of zakah, and the believers in Allah and the Last Day — those We will give a great reward﴾ (apparent) up to his saying:

Messengers as bearers of good news, [announcing] reward for obedience, and as warners, [warning] of punishment for disobedience, so that people would have no argument against God after the messengers [had come]. They would otherwise say: "You did not send us any messenger to teach us Your religion," so We sent the messengers to cut off their excuse.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 166:

﴿But Allah bears witness﴾ It was revealed when the Jews, when they were asked about the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), said: "We do not testify to that." So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But Allah bears witness﴾, i.e., He makes clear your prophethood ﴿through what He has sent down to you﴾ of the Qur'an and its proofs, ﴿He has sent it down with His knowledge﴾, i.e., He knows that you are worthy of its being sent down to you, because of your standing by it. ﴿And the angels bear witness﴾ to your prophethood, even if the Jews deny it. The witness of the angels is only recognised through the manifestation of a miracle; whoever's miracle is manifest, the angels bear witness to his truthfulness. ﴿And Allah suffices as a witness﴾, i.e., Allah suffices as a witness.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 168:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved﴾ meaning the Jews, ﴿and wronged﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ) by concealing his description, ﴿Allah would never forgive them﴾ this refers to those whom He knew would die in disbelief, ﴿nor would He guide them to a path﴾ nor would He guide them to the religion of Islam.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 169:

﴿Except the path of Hell﴾. That is, the path of Judaism, which is the way that leads them to Hell. ﴿Abiding therein forever. And that is ever easy for Allah﴾. That is, their abiding [in Hell] is easy for Allah, because nothing is difficult for Him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 170:

﴿O mankind﴾ means: the polytheists. ﴿The Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth﴾ with the guidance and the truthfulness ﴿from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you﴾ meaning: come to what is better for you than disbelief, by believing in him. ﴿But if you disbelieve﴾ you deny Muhammad and reject God's blessing upon you through him. ﴿Then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ meaning: you do not harm anyone except yourselves, because Allah is free of need of you. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing﴾ of what you will come to, whether belief or disbelief, ﴿Wise﴾ in His obligation, along with His knowledge of what will come from you.

O People of the Book, ﴿do not go to extremes﴾ (he means the Christians), ﴿in your religion, and do not say about God except the truth.﴾ That is: do not exceed the limit, and do not be excessive in your religion. ﴿...﴾ So He has no son, no wife, and no partner. As for His saying ﴿and His word which He conveyed to Mary﴾, it means that He said to him, "Be," and he was. ﴿And a spirit from Him﴾, that is: a spirit created by His command. ﴿And do not say, "Three."﴾ That is: do not say, "Our gods are three," meaning their saying: God, His consort, and His son, exalted is God above that. ﴿Cease; it is better for you.﴾ That is: bring about the cessation from this, which is better for you than what you are upon.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 172:

﴿The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels who are near (to Allah)﴾ The one whom you claim to be a god will not be too proud to be a servant of Allah, ﴿nor the angels who are near (to Allah)﴾ from the honour of Allah, the Exalted, and they are more numerous than mankind.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 174:

﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord﴾ meaning: the Prophet (peace be upon him), ﴿and We have sent down to you a clear light﴾ which is the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 175:

﴿Then as for those who believed in Allah and held fast to Him﴾, that is: they guarded themselves by obeying Him from the deviation of the Shaytan (Satan). ﴿He will admit them into mercy from Him﴾, meaning: Paradise. ﴿And bounty﴾, which He will bestow upon them with what has not occurred to their hearts. ﴿And guide them to Himself on a straight path﴾, meaning: a straight religion.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 4, verse 176:

﴿They ask you for a legal ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah (one who dies without descendants or ascendants)﴾ concerning one who dies leaving neither child nor parent. ﴿If a man dies leaving no child, and he has a sister﴾ He means: nor parent; he suffices with mentioning one of them, because it is the kalalah. ﴿And he has a sister﴾, meaning: a full sister or a sister from the father, because mention of the maternal sibling has already passed at the beginning of the surah. ﴿For her is half of what he left, and he inherits from her﴾ The brother inherits the whole estate from the sister. ﴿If she has no child. And if there are two sisters﴾ That is, the two sisters ﴿then for them are two-thirds of what he left. And if they are siblings, men and women﴾ full siblings or siblings from the father ﴿for the male, the equivalent of the share of two females﴾ ). And His saying: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ That is: so that you do not go astray, or out of dislike that you should go astray. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ regarding the division of inheritances.
